Subject: Allocation of Third-Party IP Risk & Evidence Ownership — Thermion MSA

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching our latest MSA redlines (Thermion_MSA_redlines_v3.docx) and a short evidence checklist for the typical IP notice flow (EvidenceChecklist.xlsx). I wanted to surface two narrow pain points your team called out and propose an approach that should be operationally simple for both sides:

1) Defense vs. pass-through for third-party infringement claims: your team prefers a pass-through model where Thermion handles litigation but seeks reimbursement where Redwood is deemed responsible. We heard that and want to offer a middle path to avoid a prolonged redline fight.

2) Evidence custody & technical artifacts: you asked for clarity about who retains forensic artifacts (logs, sample inputs, model version snapshots) during a notice window. Redwood's position is we should hold short-term custody for preservation while the parties coordinate handback and privilege review.

Proposed next steps:
- Quick legal alignment: Kimberly, can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a limited pass-through for third-party claims with a defend-option for claims where Redwood’s output directly infringes (narrowly defined)?
- Operational SLA: Dana / Liam, can Thermion commit to a 5-business-day initial evidence request turnaround and a single shared S3 staging location for artifacts?
- If legal aligns, I’ll prepare a single redline that implements the hybrid approach and circulate for sign-off; hoping to keep this in the DocuSign path this week.

High level ask from Thermion: expedited countersign so we can onboard next month.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Allocation of Third-Party IP Risk & Evidence Ownership — Thermion MSA

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the materials. The Thermion legal team reviewed the redlines and we do have two concrete concerns:

• Our principle is that for third-party IP claims related to model output, Thermion will defend and Redwood will reimburse only if Redwood is adjudicated responsible. We do not accept broad "right to control" language that would force us into litigation management for customer-facing uses without a finding of Redwood culpability.

• On the evidence side, we can agree to a shared staging location for forensic artifacts but cannot hand over raw customer content outside of our SOC boundary. Instead, we propose a two-step handback: (a) staged artifacts with customer identifiers redacted; (b) full artifacts provided only through a counsel-to-counsel privileged channel on proffer of a valid notice.

On the operational SLAs, 5 business days for initial intake is reasonable. However, our external counsel also asks for a narrowly tailored definition of "Model Output" to avoid cross-claim exposure from user-provided prompts.

If Redwood can: (1) accept a pass-through defense model with a reimbursement path upon final adjudication, and (2) adopt the two-step evidence handback (staging + counsel-only full access), Thermion will move forward with the procurement signature.

Dana Reed
Senior Counsel, Thermion AI
dana.reed@thermion.ai

Team —

Thanks for the clear summary, Jordan, and thanks Dana for the helpful constraints from Thermion counsel. I reviewed the options and recommend we propose a hybrid compromise that keeps the deal moving but preserves Redwood’s commercial risk profile. Key points below plus suggested redline text you can paste into the MSA:

Recommended commercial compromise (high level):
- For third-party infringement claims alleging that Redwood-generated output infringes a third party, Redwood will have the option to assume defense ("Right to Defend") where Redwood reasonably determines the claim arises solely from Redwood’s models or pre-processing; if Redwood does not assume defense within 15 business days after notice, Thermion may defend and Redwood agrees to reimburse final adjudicated damages and reasonable costs.
- For claims that primarily arise from customer-provided prompts, Thermion will retain the defense obligation (pass-through).
- Evidence custody: agree on a shared, encrypted staging area under Thermion’s control for initial artifacts with limited retention (90 days). Full artifacts will be produced counsel-to-counsel only on receipt of a valid notice and narrowly scoped subpoena or court order. Redwood will provide model hashes, inference timestamps, and model-config snapshots on request to aid triage.
- Cap/Offset: propose a mutual cap carveout for IP claims tied to insurance limits; otherwise general liability caps remain as negotiated.

Suggested redline snippet (editable):
"
Indemnification — Third Party Claims. If a third party asserts that Model Output generated by Redwood infringes such third party's intellectual property rights, Redwood shall have the right, within fifteen (15) business days of written notice, to assume sole control of the defense and settlement of such claim ("Right to Defend"). If Redwood elects not to assume defense within such period, Customer may assume defense and Redwood shall be obligated to reimburse Customer for any damages finally awarded against Customer and reasonable costs of defense. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer remains responsible for claims arising from Customer-provided prompts or data.

Evidence Custody and Production. Customer shall maintain the initial staging area for technical artifacts. Redwood may request, and Customer shall provide upon counsel-to-counsel request, non-redacted artifacts required for litigation subject to applicable privacy laws, redaction of customer PII, and a valid subpoena or order. Redwood will supply model-identifying metadata (model hash, version, inference timestamp) to facilitate triage upon request.
"

Operational asks to Thermion (please confirm):
1) Commitment to maintain a shared S3 staging bucket and a 90-day retention window for artifacts.
2) Agreement to cross-check any proposed definition of "Model Output" to ensure it excludes user-provided content.

If Thermion confirms (1) and (2), we can push a single clean redline this afternoon and route to DocuSign. Ben/Laura — be ready to accelerate procurement once Thermion confirms; we should target signature by Friday.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
